text:
jess: Hey support — quick escalation. Customer AcmeMaps (acct acme-maps, org 6743) is seeing repeated 429s nightly around 02:00 UTC during a 2h batch ingest. They're on the paid Growth plan (50k tokens/day, concurrency cap 20). They report X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset ~900s in the response headers. Can we do a temporary burst lift or sales-assisted uplift? They need to finish a nightly reindex for a demo tomorrow.

sam: Thanks — can you paste a sample response and request-id they got? Also which endpoint are they hitting (generation, embeddings, or streaming)?

jess: Pasting the customer's repro snippet (sanitized):

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-ggml-13b","input":"...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

Response headers they pasted: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 912` and body `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":"RATELIMIT_TOKEN"}`. Request-id: `req_0a1b2c3d`

They said the traffic pattern is a bunch of parallel workers (k8s cronjob) hitting the API concurrently (burst to ~120 QPS for 10 min).

sasha: Got it. A few notes:
- Growth plan default burst headroom is limited by per-minute token and concurrency thresholds. If their job does many parallel 1k-token requests, tokens burn fast.
- Confirm they're not sharing an API key across multiple pods causing token-level throttles. The RATELIMIT_TOKEN code indicates token-scoped enforcement.
- We can do a short-term exception (burst window) for up to 24h from support but need a sales approval for anything longer.

Can you ask them to: 1) attach the exact request-id lines for 3 consecutive 429s, 2) confirm which API key is used per pod, 3) check if they have client retries throttling too (we see retry storms make things worse).

jess: Sent those asks. Customer responded with three request ids: `req_0a1b2c3d`, `req_0b2c3d4e`, `req_0c3d4e5f`. They confirm a single API key is mounted to all 12 pods. They're okay toggling to per-pod keys if needed.

maria-sales: I can support a temporary uplift. Quick Qs: what QPS and token window do they need for the 2h job? Also need billing contact + expected monthly spend if we increase quota. We can provision a scheduled bump on Dedicated or upgrade to a higher Growth tier depending on ARR.

jess: They want ~150 QPS sustained for the 10-minute peaks and estimate extra ~1.2M tokens for the nightly run (~36M tokens/month if they keep this pattern). Billing contact is alice@acmemaps.com.

sasha: Two suggested short-term mitigations before sales uplifts:
- Spread work with jitter and exponential backoff for 429s (client-side).
- Implement per-pod API keys so token-level limits are distributed.
- Use batch requests where possible (combine inputs so fewer calls).

Also note: header `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min` suggests token-level cap; if requests have 1k tokens each, that quickly hits the cap.

tom: From eng side: we can temporarily whitelist their org for a burst window for 24h. However, this is manual and needs ops sign-off (and we need to set a hard cutoff). For longer-term, recommend either Dedicated capacity or increasing their Growth tier. I'll open an internal ops change but need ticket + sales signoff.

deploy-bot: Created support ticket S-2026-4873 and escalation task OPS-9987 to request a 24h burst exception for org 6743.

maria-sales: I'll reach out to alice now and coordinate a signed short-term addendum. If they expect ~36M tokens/month, that'll push them into the next pricing band; recommend sizing a committed capacity quote. I'll update the support ticket with commercial notes. :+1:

lee: Customer success here — I'll schedule a 15-min call for tomorrow 01:30 UTC to walk the customer through per-pod keys + retry/backoff patterns. Can someone from eng be on the call?

jess: Thanks everyone — I've linked the request ids and the customer's billing contact to S-2026-4873. Please add any runbooks or docs links we should send: https://docs.redwood.ai/rate-limits and https://docs.redwood.ai/best-practices/retries

sasha: I'll drop a short checklist in the ticket: 1) rotate to per-pod keys, 2) add jitter/backoff, 3) reduce max_tokens where feasible, 4) enable batching. After the call, if they still need higher throughput we'll push the sales uplift path.

maria-sales: Update: alice confirmed budget approval for a 30-day elevated window while we evaluate Dedicated. Scheduling contract addendum now.

jess: Closing the loop with customer — they implemented per-pod keys + backoff and saw failed requests drop from 14% to under 1% in a test. They'll still want the 24h uplift tonight to finish the backfill. Ops, can we enable the burst window starting 21:00 UTC for 24h and auto-revert?

tom: Ops approved the temporary uplift for 24h starting 21:00 UTC; will auto-revert. Logged in OPS-9987. Monitor metrics and we'll rollback early if any system pressure.

lee: Call scheduled, invite sent. :calendar:

jess: Thanks team — marking support thread as resolved pending uplift. 

(emoji reactions: :white_check_mark:, :rocket:)
